minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee dropped the write-in minimum-vote idea and ranked-choice voting; term limits go to a survey.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed a draft revised Charter section by section, mostly on the town manager's appointment and supervision powers. It dropped the write-in minimum-vote proposal and ranked-choice voting, and left term limits for a survey. The town clerk appointed-versus-elected question was straw-polled informally and left open, and extra meetings were set before the warrant closes.

what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee dropped ranked-choice voting from the list of items under consideration.
The committee moved term limits to a survey instead of deciding them at the meeting.
A show of hands on whether to keep considering the write-in minimum-vote proposal was held; the count was not audible, and the idea was not continued.
The town manager search committee is to add one registered-voter member of the public, appointed by the moderator.
Extra meetings were proposed on the 7th and 14th to finish a draft before the warrant closes.

why_it_matters: The Charter sets how the town is run, including how the town manager is hired and supervised, and any changes need a Town Meeting vote, so the draft shapes what voters will be asked to approve.
Term limits and the town clerk question (appointed or elected) remain open, so residents can still weigh in through the survey and later meetings before a draft reaches the warrant.
